objective: Add a module `demo_app/table.py` with a function `render_table(headers: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str` that renders a plain-text table. Cells are single-line strings; a cell's width is `len(cell)`. The width of a column is the largest width among its header and all its row cells. Every column is left-aligned: each cell is padded on the right with spaces to its column width. Output lines, in order: the header line, a separator line, then one line per row in the given order. The header line and each row line are the padded cells joined with ` | ` (space, pipe, space). The separator line is `-` repeated column-width times for each column, joined with `-+-`. After a line is built, all trailing space characters are removed from its end, so no line ends with a space (this also applies when the last cells are empty). The lines are joined with `\n` and the output has no trailing newline. With no rows, the output is just the header line and the separator line. A row whose number of cells differs from the number of headers (shorter or longer) raises `ValueError`. Callers always pass at least one header.
acceptance: The column width grows to fit a cell that is wider than its header, and a header that is wider than every cell
render_table(['x'], []) returns 'x\n-' (header line plus separator, single column, no ' | ' or '-+-')
No line has trailing spaces, including a last column that is padded (for example a short last-column cell under a wider one) or empty
The output does not end with a newline and lines are separated by a single '\n'
A row with fewer or more cells than headers raises ValueError, including when there are other valid rows
